name: Zibia
overview: Zibia is a male member of the tribe of Benjamin, uniquely identified as the son of Shaharaim according to 1 Chronicles 8:9. Beyond this genealogical detail, Scripture provides limited information about his life or role. His mention serves primarily to establish lineage within the Benjaminite tribe.
namesAndTitles: The name Zibia is a proper name meaning "gazelle," reflecting a common biblical practice of using animal imagery in personal names. There is no indication that this name was given directly by God, but it carries the connotation of grace or swiftness associated with the gazelle.
familyAndRelationships: Zibia is recorded as the son of Shaharaim and the brother of Hodesh, as inferred from the genealogical listing in 1 Chronicles 8:9. Scripture does not provide further family details beyond these relationships.
scriptureSignificance: Zibia's significance lies in his place within the genealogical records of the tribe of Benjamin, which help trace the heritage and tribal organization of Israel. His mention underscores the biblical emphasis on family lineage as foundational to God's covenant people. While not prominent in narrative events, his inclusion preserves the continuity of God's chosen tribe.
